For purposes of these Guidelines, \"year\" of experience is determined by the number of years elapsed since the timekeeper\'s admission to the bar in any jurisdiction. Time spent in judicial clerkships counts toward years of experience. Time spent in non-legal positions does not count unless the GC agrees otherwise in writing.
These rate caps are absolute ceilings. No timekeeper may bill the Company at a rate exceeding the applicable cap regardless of the timekeeper\'s standard rate, experience, qualifications, reputation, or the complexity of the matter. Invoices containing rates in excess of these caps will be automatically reduced by Lexera Solutions to the applicable cap rate, and the firm will not be entitled to recover the difference. The Company will not negotiate exceptions to the rate caps on a timekeeper-by-timekeeper basis except in extraordinary circumstances approved in advance and in writing by the GC. Firms should not propose or include rates exceeding these caps in engagement letters, staffing plans, or budget submissions.
**[3.2 Annual Rate Increases]**
Outside counsel may request annual rate increases effective January 1 of each calendar year, subject to the following conditions:
**(a) Maximum Annual Increase.** Annual rate increases shall not exceed three percent (3%) of the prior year\'s approved rate for any individual timekeeper. Requests for increases in excess of 3% require a detailed written justification explaining the basis for the requested increase --- including changes in the timekeeper\'s experience, responsibility, or market conditions --- and the advance written approval of the GC. Absent such approval, the maximum rate increase for any timekeeper shall be capped at 3% of the prior year\'s approved rate. For the avoidance of doubt, the 3% cap is calculated on a per-timekeeper basis, not as a blended or average increase across the staffing team.
**(b) Advance Written Notice.** Requests for rate increases must be submitted in writing to the GC no later than sixty (60) days prior to the proposed effective date of the increase. Rate increase requests that do not comply with this notice requirement may be denied in their entirety at the GC\'s discretion, without obligation to provide a reason for denial. For rate increases proposed to be effective January 1, the written request must be received by the GC no later than November 1 of the preceding year. Requests received after November 1 will be deemed untimely and may be rejected without further consideration, regardless of the merits of the requested increase. The Company will not consider retroactive application of rate increases for which timely notice was not provided.
**(c) Interaction with Rate Caps.** No rate increase, even if within the 3% annual cap described in subsection (a) above, may cause a timekeeper\'s rate to exceed the applicable maximum rate set forth in Section 3.1. If application of a permissible percentage increase would result in a rate exceeding the cap for the timekeeper\'s category, the rate shall be set at the cap amount. For example, if a senior associate\'s current approved rate is \$540.00 and a 3% increase would yield \$556.20, the rate would be capped at \$550.00 because that is the maximum rate for the Senior Associate category under Section 3.1.
**(d) Effective Date.** Rate increases that comply with all of the requirements set forth in subsections (a) through (c) above shall be effective on January 1 of the applicable calendar year. Retroactive rate increases are not permitted under any circumstances. Time billed prior to January 1 at the new rate will be reduced to the prior year\'s approved rate. The Company will confirm approved rate increases in writing, and no rate increase shall be considered approved until written confirmation is received from the GC or the GC\'s designee.
**[3.3 Rate Approval Process]**
All billing rates must be approved in writing by the GC or the GC\'s designee prior to the commencement of any billable work by the applicable timekeeper. Outside counsel shall submit proposed rates for all anticipated timekeepers as part of the engagement letter process described in Section 2.1. Rates for new timekeepers added to a matter after the commencement of the engagement must be submitted for approval concurrent with the timekeeper addition notice required under Section 4.3. The Company reserves the right to negotiate rates below the caps set forth in Section 3.1, and outside counsel should not assume that rates at the cap levels will be automatically approved. Approved rates for each timekeeper shall be documented in the engagement letter, a rate schedule amendment thereto, or other written confirmation from the GC. In the absence of written rate approval, the Company reserves the right to pay at the rate it deems appropriate, up to but not exceeding the applicable rate cap.
**[3.4 Blended and Alternative Rates]**
The Company may, in its sole discretion, propose or agree to blended rates, fixed fees, capped fees, phased fees, success-based arrangements, or other alternative fee arrangements for specific matters, phases of matters, or categories of work. Any such arrangement must be documented in a written agreement signed by the GC, and the terms of such agreement shall supplement (but not replace) these Guidelines except to the extent expressly stated in the written agreement. In the absence of a written alternative fee agreement applicable to a particular matter, standard hourly billing at approved rates shall apply to all services rendered on that matter.
No success fees, contingency arrangements, premium billing, risk premiums, performance bonuses, or other non-standard fee enhancements of any kind shall be charged to the Company without an express written agreement signed by both the Chief Executive Officer and the General Counsel of Colton Beverage. Any invoice that includes a success fee, premium, or bonus charge absent such a dual-signed agreement will be rejected in its entirety and returned for correction.
**[SECTION 4 --- STAFFING]**
**[4.1 Staffing Principles]**
Outside counsel shall staff all matters efficiently and in a manner consistent with the complexity, risk, and value of the matter to the Company. The Company expects lean staffing with appropriate leverage, meaning that work should be performed by the lowest-cost timekeeper with the skills and experience necessary to perform the work competently and efficiently. Overstaffing, duplicative attendance at meetings, hearings, or depositions, and unnecessary layering of review --- such as multiple levels of associate and partner review of routine work product --- will result in reductions to invoiced amounts. Outside counsel should endeavor to assign work at the appropriate level and to avoid the use of senior timekeepers for tasks that can be competently performed by more junior attorneys or paralegals.
**[4.2 Partner Staffing Limitations]**
No more than two (2) partners may bill on any single matter without prior written approval from the GC. This limitation includes equity partners, non-equity partners, and of counsel with partner-level billing rates (i.e., rates at or above the Non-Equity Partner cap of \$725.00 per hour). The responsible partner identified in the engagement letter counts as one of the two permitted partners. If the approved staffing plan includes fewer than two partners and the firm wishes to add a partner to the matter, the firm must obtain advance written approval from the GC before the additional partner begins any billable work on the matter. Time billed by a third or subsequent partner (or by any unapproved partner) will be written off at the firm\'s expense and will not be paid by the Company, regardless of the value or quality of the services rendered.
**[4.3 Timekeeper Addition and Substitution]**
No timekeeper may be added to or substituted on a matter without (a) at least ten (10) business days\' advance written notice to the GC, and (b) the GC\'s written approval of the addition or substitution. The written notice must include the following information for the proposed timekeeper: (i) full name; (ii) title or position within the firm; (iii) year of bar admission and years of relevant experience; (iv) proposed billing rate, which must comply with the applicable rate cap under Section 3.1; (v) qualifications, background, and experience relevant to the matter; and (vi) a description of the anticipated role and responsibilities on the matter.
Time billed by a timekeeper who has not been properly noticed and approved in accordance with this Section 4.3 will not be paid. The Company will not reimburse the firm for any such time, and the firm bears the full risk and cost of commencing work with an unapproved timekeeper.
The ten (10) business day requirement is strictly enforced. Compressed notice periods will be considered only in genuinely exigent circumstances --- such as the unexpected departure of a key team member during a critical phase of the matter --- and only if accompanied by a contemporaneous written explanation of the exigent circumstances. Such compressed-notice requests require the GC\'s express approval. The GC\'s agreement to a compressed notice period in one instance do

es not constitute a waiver of the ten-business-day requirement for future timekeeper additions or substitutions. Outside counsel is encouraged to plan staffing needs in advance and to submit timekeeper addition requests well before the proposed timekeeper is expected to begin work.
**[4.4 Staffing Efficiency Ratio]**
To promote cost efficiency and appropriate leverage, the Company requires that at least forty percent (40%) of total attorney hours on any matter be performed by associates at or below the fifth-year level (i.e., 1st through 5th year associates, including junior and mid-level associates as categorized in Section 3.1). For purposes of this calculation, partner hours, senior associate hours (6th year and above), and of counsel hours are excluded from the numerator but included in the denominator. Paralegal and legal assistant hours are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator. The formula is expressed as follows:
**Staffing Efficiency Ratio = (Junior Associate Hours + Mid-Level Associate Hours) ÷ (Total Attorney Hours) ≥ 40%**
The staffing efficiency ratio shall be calculated on a cumulative basis --- i.e., from the inception of the engagement through the measurement date --- and reviewed at each quarterly budget review. Outside counsel should monitor the ratio on an ongoing basis and adjust staffing as necessary to maintain compliance. Persistent failure to meet the 40% threshold may result in a rate reduction applied to senior timekeeper hours for the underperforming period, the amount of which shall be determined by the GC in consultation with outside counsel.
**[4.5 Diversity Staffing Requirements]**
Colton Beverage is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion in the legal profession and believes that diverse legal teams produce better outcomes for clients and contribute to a more equitable profession. The Company requires that each matter team include at least one diverse attorney in a \"significant role.\" For purposes of these Guidelines, a \"significant role\" is defined as an attorney who bills fifteen percent (15%) or more of total attorney hours on the matter (excluding paralegal and legal assistant hours from the calculation). \"Diverse attorney\" includes, without limitation, attorneys who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, individuals with disabilities, and veterans, as those terms are commonly understood in the legal profession.
Outside counsel shall report diversity staffing metrics --- including the name, role, diversity category (to the extent voluntarily disclosed by the individual), and percentage of total hours for each diverse attorney --- in each quarterly budget report and upon request by the GC. The Company recognizes that diversity information is sensitive and personal and will treat all such information as confidential. The Company may, in its discretion, adjust engagement decisions and matter allocations based on a firm\'s demonstrated commitment to diversity staffing.
**[SECTION 5 --- BUDGETING]**
**[5.1 Budget Requirements]**
Outside counsel must submit a detailed matter budget for every matter with an anticipated total cost (fees plus expenses) exceeding Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$50,000). Budgets must be submitted within thirty (30) days of the date of engagement and must be updated quarterly or whenever material changes in scope, strategy, or anticipated expenditures occur. Updated budgets should be submitted concurrently with the quarterly matter status report described in Section 9.1. Budgets must be organized by UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) litigation or counseling phase codes, as applicable to the matter type. Matters with anticipated costs below \$50,000 do not require a formal budget but are still subject to all other provisions of these Guidelines, including rate caps, staffing requirements, and expense policies.
**[5.2 Budget Format and Content]**
Each budget shall include, at a minimum, the following components:
> \(a\) A phase-by-phase fee estimate using standard UTBMS codes (e.g., L100 through L700 for litigation matters, as set forth in Appendix A), with estimated fees broken out for each phase and a total fee estimate;
>
> \(b\) A staffing table showing each timekeeper who is expected to work on the matter, including their name, title, role on the matter, approved billing rate, and estimated hours by phase, with total estimated hours and fees for each timekeeper;
>
> \(c\) A detailed expense budget with line items broken out by category (e.g., e-discovery, expert witnesses, travel, court costs, deposition costs, document reproduction, and other expenses), with estimated amounts for each category and a total expense estimate;
>
> \(d\) A narrative description of key assumptions underlying the budget, including the anticipated litigation strategy, expected duration, key milestones and deadlines, significant risk factors that could affect the budget, and any contingencies or alternative scenarios that may warrant budget adjustments; and
>
> \(e\) A grand total that reconciles all estimated fees and expenses into a single total projected cost for the matter.
The fee total derived from the phase-by-phase breakdown (component (a)) must reconcile to the fee total derived from the staffing table (component (b), calculated as hours multiplied by rates). Any discrepancy between these two calculations must be identified and explained in the budget narrative. Budgets that do not reconcile will be returned for revision and will not be approved until the discrepancy is resolved. The Company expects outside counsel to exercise professional judgment and diligence in preparing budgets and to avoid both unduly optimistic estimates and excessive padding.
**[5.3 Budget Variance and Overruns]**
Outside counsel must manage all matters within the approved budget. Budget discipline is a critical component of the Company\'s legal spend management program, and the Company expects outside counsel to treat approved budgets as binding commitments, not aspirational targets. Any single phase that is projected to exceed one hundred ten percent (110%) of its budgeted amount requires advance written notice to and approval from the GC before additional fees in excess of the 110% threshold will be paid. The notice must include an explanation of the reason for the overrun, the revised estimated cost for the phase, and any recommended adjustments to the overall budget.
Failure to provide timely notice of a budget overrun --- i.e., notice provided after the 110% threshold has already been exceeded --- may result in non-payment of fees incurred above 110% of the budgeted phase amount. The Company will conduct quarterly budget-to-actual reviews and expects outside counsel to proactively monitor and report variances between budgeted and actual expenditures as part of the quarterly reporting process described in Section 9.1.
**[5.4 Post-Trial and Appellate Reserves]**
Budgets shall not include reserves or estimated fees for post-trial motions or appeals unless the client has expressly requested appellate planning in writing. The Company\'s standard practice is to evaluate post-trial and appellate strategy on a case-by-case basis at the conclusion of the trial phase, and outside counsel should not presume that appellate work will be authorized. Any such reserve, if requested by the client, must be presented as a separate line item with its own detailed assumptions and approval process, distinct from the trial-phase budget. The post-trial/appellate reserve requires independent GC approval and must be justified by a written memorandum from outside counsel addressing the likelihood of post-trial motions or appeal, the estimated costs, and the recommended strategy.
Inclusion of an unauthorized post-trial or appellate reserve in a budget submission --- i.e., a reserve for post-trial motions or appeals that was not expressly requested by the Company --- will result in the budget being returned for revision, and the reserve amount will not be approved until and unless the GC specifically authorizes appellate planning for the matter. Use of UTBMS code L700 (Post-Trial Motions and Appeal) is subject to these restrictions.
**[SECTION 6 --- BILLING PRACTICES]**
**[6.1 Billing Frequency]**
Outside counsel shall submit invoices on a monthly basis, within fifteen (15) calendar days of the end of each calendar month for which services were rendered. For example, invoices for services rendered during the month of January must be submitted no later than February 15. Timely invoice submission is essential to the Company\'s financial planning and reporting obligations. Payment terms are net forty-five (45) days from the Company\'s receipt of a compliant invoice. Invoices that do not comply with these Guidelines --- including invoices that contain billing errors, lack required codes, or include non-compliant charges --- will be returned for correction, and the forty-five (45) day payment period restarts upon receipt of the corrected and compliant invoice. Late invoices --- i.e., invoices submitted more than sixty (60) days after the end of the applicable billing period --- may be rejected at the Company\'s discretion.
**[6.2 UTBMS Codes]**
All invoices must use UTBMS task-based billing codes. Each time entry must include the applicable UTBMS activity code corresponding to the phase and task performed. The Company uses standard UTBMS litigation codes for litigation matters (see Appendix A) and standard UTBMS counseling codes for transactional and advisory matters. Invoices that lack UTBMS codes, that use incorrect or inapplicable codes, or that fail to code individual entries will be rejected and returned for correction. Outside counsel should ensure that all timekeepers are trained in the proper use of UTBMS codes and that billing entries are coded at the time of entry, not retroactively.
**[6.3 Block Billing Prohibition]**
Block billing is strictly prohibited. Each time entry must describe a single task or activity, performed by a single timekeeper, with sufficient detail and specificity to allow Lexera Solutions and the Company to evaluate the reasonableness of the time charged and to associate the entry with the appropriate UTBMS code and budget phase. Entries that combine multiple tasks into a single time entry (e.g., \"Research, draft motion, and conference with partner --- 4.5 hours\") will be reduced or rejected because they do not permit meaningful review of the time allocated to each component task. Similarly, vague or generic entries (e.g., \"Legal research\" or \"Work on case\") do not satisfy the specificity requirement and will be reduced or rejected.
Minimum billing increments shall be in tenths of an hour (0.1 hour, or six minutes). Minimum charges that exceed the actual time expended are not permitted. For example, a five-minute telephone call should be billed as 0.1 hours, not rounded up to 0.2 or 0.3 hours. The Company expects all timekeepers to record time contemporaneously and accurately.
**[6.4 Non-Billable Activities]**
The following activities are not billable to the Company and will not be paid, regardless of the timekeeper performing the activity or the time expended:
> \(a\) Time spent preparing, reviewing, revising, or correcting invoices or billing statements, including time spent responding to billing inquiries from Lexera Solutions;
>
> \(b\) Time spent on conflicts checks, including initial and supplemental conflicts searches and analysis;
>
> \(c\) Administrative tasks, including filing, organizing, indexing, or cataloguing documents, whether in physical or electronic form;
>
> \(d\) Time for intra-firm training, education, continuing legal education, mentoring, or professional development, even if the training relates to the subject matter of the Company\'s matter;
>
> \(e\) Travel time, except with prior written GC approval for travel exceeding four (4) hours in duration for a single trip, in which case the approved travel time shall be billed at fifty percent (50%) of the applicable timekeeper\'s approved rate;
>
> \(f\) Time for multiple attorneys attending the same internal firm meeting, conference call, or strategy session unless the attendance of multiple attorneys has been pre-approved in writing by the GC, who must be informed of the purpose of the meeting and the reason multiple attorneys are required;
>
> \(g\) Proofreading and cite-checking by attorneys billed at attorney rates, which tasks should be performed by paralegals, legal assistants, or support staff at the applicable lower rates; and
>
> \(h\) Time spent \"getting up to speed\" due to timekeeper transitions, including time for new timekeepers to review the file, unless the transition was requested by the Company.
**[6.5 Multiple Timekeeper Attendance]**
Without prior written GC approval, the Company will pay for only one (1) attorney to attend any court hearing, deposition, client meeting, mediation session, or other proceeding (other than trial). If outside counsel believes that the attendance of more than one attorney is necessary or advisable for a particular proceeding, the firm must request and obtain the GC\'s advance written approval. The request must explain the reason multiple attorneys are needed and identify the attorneys who would attend. Similarly, no more than two (2) attorneys may attend any trial session without the GC\'s advance written pre-approval. Invoices reflecting multiple timekeeper attendance at a proceeding without prior approval will be reduced to reflect only the single lowest-rate attorney\'s time, and the time of all other attorneys in attendance will be disallowed.
**[SECTION 7 --- EXPENSES]**
**[7.1 General Expense Policy]**
Outside counsel is expected to manage expenses prudently and in a manner consistent with the standards the Company applies to its own internal expenditures. All expenses must be reasonable in amount, necessary to the matter, and directly related to the legal services being provided. The Company reserves the right to reject or reduce any expense that it deems excessive, unnecessary, duplicative, or non-compliant with these Guidelines. All expenses exceeding Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000) in a single category for a single monthly invoice must be documented with supporting invoices, receipts, or other written substantiation. Expenses below the \$5,000 threshold should be supported by documentation upon request. Outside counsel should exercise judgment in incurring expenses and should err on the side of consulting the GC before incurring significant or unusual expenditures.
**[7.2 E-Discovery and Technology Expenses]**
**(a) Competitive Bidding Requirement.** E-discovery vendor costs that are estimated to exceed Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) over the life of a matter require competitive bidding among at least three (3) qualified vendors prior to vendor selection. Outside counsel must submit documentation of the competitive bidding process --- including the names of all bidding vendors, their proposals or cost estimates, the evaluation criteria used, and the basis for selection of the recommended vendor --- to the GC for review and approval before engaging the selected vendor. Sole-source engagements for e-discovery services exceeding the \$200,000 threshold are not permitted without express written GC approval, which must be supported by documented justification for the sole-source selection explaining why competitive bidding was impracticable or not in the Company\'s interest.
**(b) Monthly Reporting.** Outside counsel shall include a monthly summary of e-discovery costs --- broken out by hosting, processing, review platform licensing, document review (including contract review attorneys), and production --- with each monthly invoice. This summary shall include cumulative totals for the life of the matter and a comparison to the budgeted amounts for e-discovery.
**(c) Vendor Management.** The Company reserves the right to designate preferred e-discovery vendors for use on Company matters. If the Company has designated a preferred vendor for a particular service (e.g., document hosting, processing, or review platform), outside counsel must use the designated vendor unless an exception is approved in writing by the GC. The Company may negotiate volume-based pricing or other favorable terms with preferred vendors, and outside counsel is expected to facilitate the use of such vendors.
**[7.3 Expert Witnesses and Consultants]**
**(a) Pre-Approval Threshold.** Expert witness and consultant fees that are estimated to exceed Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$75,000) per expert or consultant over the life of the matter require the GC\'s pre-approval before the expert or consultant is retained. The pre-approval request must include: (i) the proposed expert\'s or consultant\'s curriculum vitae; (ii) a detailed proposed scope of work describing the tasks the expert will be asked to perform; (iii) the expert\'s or consultant\'s complete fee schedule, including hourly rates, flat fees (if applicable), and estimated total fees through the completion of the engagement; and (iv) a written justification for the selection of the proposed expert, including the expert\'s qualifications, relevant experience, and any prior engagements with the firm or the Company. Outside counsel should submit the pre-approval request sufficiently in advance of the anticipated retention date to allow the GC a reasonable period for review. Retention of an expert or consultant without required pre-approval may result in non-reimbursement of the expert\'s fees.
**(b) Number of Experts.** The engagement of more than two (2) testifying experts on any single matter requires the GC\'s pre-approval. The request for approval must explain the need for additional testifying experts and describe how the proposed experts\' testimony will be non-duplicative and necessary to the Company\'s case.
**(c) Expert Reports.** Draft expert reports must be shared with the GC for review and comment at least fifteen (15) business days before the applicable submission deadline. Outside counsel should coordinate with the GC to ensure that expert reports are consistent with the Company\'s litigation strategy and that the GC has an adequate opportunity to provide input before the report is finalized.
**[7.4 Travel]**
**(a) Air Travel.** Air travel is reimbursed at economy/coach class only. First class and business class travel require advance written pre-approval from the GC, which will be granted only in extraordinary circumstances (e.g., international flights exceeding eight hours in duration where economy seating is unavailable, or documented medical necessity). Absent such pre-approval, reimbursement will be limited to the lowest available economy class fare for the same route and dates, and the firm shall bear the difference between the economy fare and the actual fare paid. Outside counsel must submit documentation of the economy fare comparison when seeking reimbursement for any air travel.
**(b) Ground Transportation.** Rental cars (mid-size class or below), taxis, and ride-share services (e.g., Uber, Lyft) are reimbursable at actual cost. Limousine service, black car service, or other premium ground transportation is not reimbursable without the GC\'s advance written pre-approval. Parking fees and tolls incurred in connection with matter-related travel are reimbursable at actual cost.
**(c) Hotels.** Hotel accommodations are reimbursable at reasonable market rates, not to exceed Two Hundred Seventy-Five Dollars (\$275) per night in major metropolitan areas (defined as the fifty largest U.S. metropolitan statistical areas) and Two Hundred Dollars (\$200) per night in all other locations. Suites, room upgrades, resort fees not included in the base room rate, and minibar charges are not reimbursable. Outside counsel should make reservations at re

asonably priced hotels and should avoid luxury or boutique properties unless the rate falls within the applicable nightly cap.
**(d) Meals.** Meals during business travel are reimbursable up to Seventy-Five Dollars (\$75) per day per person. Receipts are required for individual meals exceeding \$25. Alcohol is not reimbursable under any circumstances, whether incurred during travel or otherwise.
**(e) General.** Outside counsel should seek the most cost-effective travel arrangements available and should book air travel and hotel accommodations at least fourteen (14) days in advance where practicable. Advance planning reduces travel costs and is expected. The Company does not reimburse personal travel expenses, travel insurance, or loyalty program fees.
**[7.5 Copying, Printing, and Document Reproduction]**
Internal copying, printing, and document reproduction costs are not reimbursable. These charges are considered ordinary overhead costs that are included in and compensated by the firm\'s hourly rates. Only third-party copying or printing costs --- i.e., costs charged by an outside vendor for large-scale document reproduction, trial exhibit preparation, bulk printing, or similar services that are beyond the firm\'s ordinary internal capabilities --- are reimbursable, and only when accompanied by supporting third-party invoices. Any claim for reimbursement of copying, printing, or document reproduction costs must clearly identify the third-party vendor by name, the matter-related purpose of the reproduction, the volume reproduced, and the per-page or per-unit cost charged by the vendor. Claims for internal copying, printing, or document reproduction costs --- regardless of how they are labeled or described on the invoice --- will be rejected and removed from the invoice.
**[7.6 Court Costs and Filing Fees]**
Court filing fees, service of process costs, pro hac vice admission fees, and other court-imposed costs and charges are reimbursable at actual cost, provided that supporting documentation (e.g., court receipts, process server invoices) is submitted with the invoice. Outside counsel should use the most cost-effective method of service available and should not engage premium or expedited service providers unless the circumstances of the matter require it.
**[7.7 Other Expenses]**
Any expense category not specifically addressed in Sections 7.1 through 7.6 of these Guidelines and exceeding Ten Thousand Dollars (\$10,000) requires advance written GC approval before the expense is incurred. This includes, but is not limited to: jury consultants, mock trials, focus groups, litigation graphics and demonstrative exhibits, trial technology support and presentation services, private investigators, specialized database or records research, court reporters for non-deposition proceedings, and any other unusual, non-routine, or extraordinary expense. Outside counsel should contact the GC before incurring any expense that is unusual, non-routine, or that the firm has reason to believe may not be covered by these Guidelines, regardless of the dollar amount, to confirm reimbursability and avoid disputes.
The Company reserves the right to reject any expense not specifically addressed in these Guidelines if advance approval was not obtained, even if the expense would otherwise be considered reasonable and necessary. When in doubt, outside counsel should seek approval before incurring the expense.
**[7.8 Non-Reimbursable Expenses]**
The following expenses are not reimbursable under any circumstances and will be removed from any invoice on which they appear:
> \(a\) Internal copying, printing, and document reproduction costs (see Section 7.5);
>
> \(b\) Word processing charges and secretarial overtime, including charges for after-hours word processing or document preparation;
>
> \(c\) General office overhead, including postage, fax charges, local telephone charges, office supplies, and similar items;
>
> \(d\) Westlaw, LexisNexis, Bloomberg Law, or similar legal research database charges, whether billed as a flat fee, per-search charge, or time-based charge (these are considered firm overhead included in hourly rates);

> \(e\) Meals not associated with authorized business travel as described in Section 7.4(d);

All invoices must be submitted electronically through the Company\'s designated e-billing platform in LEDES 1998B format. **[SECTION 9 --- REPORTING AND COMMUNICATION]**
**[9.1 Matter Status Reports]**
Outside counsel must provide written matter status reports to the GC on a monthly basis, concurrent with invoice submission. The purpose of status reports is to keep the GC and the in-house legal team informed of developments and to facilitate proactive management of legal matters and legal spend. Each status report must include the following components:
> \(a\) A summary of activities performed during the prior month, including key work product deliverables, proceedings attended, and milestones achieved;
>
> \(b\) Key developments and upcoming deadlines, including court dates, discovery cutoffs, filing deadlines, and any other time-sensitive events;
>
> \(c\) A budget-to-actual comparison by phase, showing budgeted amounts, actual amounts invoiced to date, amounts remaining in the budget, and any projected variances;
>
> \(d\) Any staffing changes, including the addition, departure, or substitution of timekeepers, with reference to the approval process under Section 4.3;
>
> \(e\) A risk assessment and strategic recommendations, including an updated evaluation of the strengths and weaknesses of the Company\'s position, potential settlement value, and any recommended changes in strategy; and
>
> \(f\) Anticipated activities and expenditures for the next sixty (60) days, including a preview of expected work and estimated costs for the upcoming period.
**[9.2 Early Case Assessment]**
Within sixty (60) days of engagement on any litigation matter, outside counsel must deliver a written Early Case Assessment (\"ECA\") to the GC. The ECA is a critical tool for evaluating the Company\'s litigation portfolio and making informed decisions about case strategy, settlement, and resource allocation. The ECA shall include, at a minimum: an analysis of all claims and defenses; an assessment of the likelihood of success on each claim or defense; an estimate of the Company\'s potential damages exposure, including best-case, worst-case, and most-likely scenarios; identification of key risks, including evidentiary, legal, and procedural risks; an estimated duration of the matter from inception through trial; and a detailed litigation budget complying with the requirements of Section 5.
**[9.3 Material Developments]**
Outside counsel must notify the GC within twenty-four (24) hours of any material development on any matter, including but not limited to the following: adverse or significant court rulings or orders; settlement demands, offers, or counteroffers; discovery of material evidence (whether favorable or adverse); changes in opposing counsel or opposing party status; staffing changes on the matter team; actual or potential conflict issues; government investigations or regulatory inquiries related to the matter; media inquiries or public reporting related to the matter; or any other event or development reasonably likely to affect the Company\'s legal position, the matter strategy, or the budget by more than ten percent (10%). Notifications should be made by telephone followed by a written summary via email.
**[SECTION 10 --- TERMINATION]**
**[10.1 Termination Rights]**
The Company may terminate any outside counsel engagement at any time, with or without cause, upon written notice to the firm. Upon termination, outside counsel shall promptly deliver to the Company or its designee all files, work product, documents, data, and other materials in the firm\'s possession or control that relate to the Company\'s matter, including electronic files, databases, and any materials held by vendors retained by the firm in connection with the matter. The Company shall pay for services properly rendered through the date of termination in accordance with these Guidelines, subject to all billing requirements, rate caps, and other provisions herein. Outside counsel shall submit a final invoice within thirty (30) days of the termination date.
**[10.2 Transition Obligations]**
Upon termination or transition of a matter to new counsel --- whether due to termination by the Company, the firm\'s withdrawal, or any other reason --- outside counsel shall cooperate fully and in good faith in the transition of the matter. This cooperation includes, without limitation, participating in transition meetings with successor counsel, preparing a comprehensive written matter summary covering the history of the matter, key facts, pending deadlines, open issues, and strategic considerations, and making key team members available for reasonable follow-up questions during the transition period. Transition cooperation is an obligation of the engagement, and the firm shall not charge the Company for transition-related services, including the preparation of the written matter summary and participation in transition meetings.

\$285,000 reflects anticipated volumes of approximately 2.5 million documents for processing and review through the expert discovery phase. Clearpoint\'s platform supports technology-assisted review workflows that significantly reduce the cost and time required for manual document review, and their team has been responsive and effective in meeting the Court\'s discovery deadlines to date.
**5.2 Expert Witnesses (\$175,000)**
We anticipate retaining two expert witnesses in connection with this matter: (1) a damages expert to quantify the financial impact of Ridgewater\'s breach of the exclusive distribution agreement and misappropriation of Colton\'s proprietary pricing algorithms, estimated at \$90,000 for the engagement through trial testimony; and (2) a data forensics and trade secrets expert to testify regarding the methods and scope of the misappropriation of Colton\'s proprietary pricing algorithms and customer data, estimated at \$85,000. Expert selection is currently underway, and we will provide further details to the General Counsel\'s office as engagements are finalized and expert reports are prepared.
**5.3 Travel (\$68,000)**
Travel expenses include airfare, hotel, ground transportation, and meals for depositions scheduled in Atlanta, Miami, and New York, as well as court appearances in Fulton County, Georgia. Lead partner travel will be business class for depositions in Miami and New York to accommodate scheduling demands and ensure Mr. Croft is fully prepared upon arrival. Associate and paralegal travel will be economy class. Hotel accommodations will be at properties offering negotiated corporate rates where available. We will exercise reasonable judgment in minimizing travel costs while ensuring the team is adequately positioned to meet scheduling and preparation requirements.
**5.4 Mock Trial / Jury Consulting --- Silvermark Consulting Group (\$95,000)**
We recommend conducting a mock trial exercise and jury profiling study to inform trial strategy in advance of the April 6, 2026 trial date. We have identified Silvermark Consulting Group as the vendor for this engagement based on their experience with complex commercial disputes in Fulton County. The estimated cost of \$95,000 includes a full-day mock trial with two deliberating panels, post-exercise analysis and debriefing, and a supplemental jury profile analysis for the Fulton County jury pool. This exercise is expected to provide critical insights into juror perceptions of the trade secrets and breach of contract claims and guide the development of trial themes and presentation strategy.
**5.5 Copying / Printing (\$15,000)**
We estimate \$15,000 for internal document reproduction, including printing of trial binders, deposition exhibit sets, and correspondence files. This reflects the volume of materials required for a matter of this scope and complexity, particularly given the anticipated length of trial and the number of witnesses and exhibits involved.
**5.6 Other Expenses --- Filing Fees and Court Reporter (\$50,500)**
Court reporter and deposition transcript costs are estimated at \$42,000 for 12 to 15 depositions, including real-time transcription for key depositions and videography for witnesses whose testimony may be presented at trial via video. Filing fees, service of process, subpoena fees, and related court costs are estimated at \$8,500, reflecting the ongoing costs associated with motions practice, subpoena enforcement, and trial-related filings.
**[Section 6: Budget Assumptions and Qualifications]**
The budget set forth in this proposal is based on the following key assumptions and qualifications. To the extent any of these assumptions prove inaccurate or circumstances materially change, we will promptly notify the General Counsel\'s office and, if necessary, submit a budget supplement for review and approval.
1\. **Trial Schedule.** The budget assumes that trial will proceed as currently scheduled on April 6, 2026, and will last approximately 8 to 10 business days, concluding on or about April 30, 2026. No continuances or material scheduling changes are assumed.
2\. **Discovery Deadlines.** Fact discovery will close on September 30, 2025, and expert discovery will close on December 15, 2025. No extensions to these deadlines are assumed. If the Court grants discovery extensions or if the volume of discovery materially exceeds current estimates, a budget supplement may be required.
3\. **Number of Depositions.** The budget assumes 12 to 15 fact depositions and 2 to 4 expert depositions. Additional depositions necessitated by new parties, intervening discovery, or Court orders may increase costs.
4\. **Dispositive Motions.** The budget assumes one round of dispositive motions, consisting primarily of a motion for summary judgment to be filed by Colton. If multiple rounds of motion practice are required, including cross-motions for summary judgment or additional Daubert motions, hours and fees may increase beyond the budgeted amounts for Phase L400.
5\. **Boyd Whitaker\'s Potential Involvement.** Boyd Whitaker\'s potential contribution of approximately 60 hours for summary judgment briefing is referenced in the phase narrative for L400 and in the timekeeper biographies, but has not been included in the staffing totals or fee estimates, as his involvement remains subject to confirmation. Should Mr. Whitaker\'s participation be confirmed, we will provide an updated staffing and fee estimate at that time.
6\. **No Counterclaims.** The budget does not include costs associated with any counterclaims that may be filed by Ridgewater. As of the date of this submission, Ridgewater has not asserted any counterclaims. If counterclaims are filed, we will prepare and submit a budget supplement addressing the additional work required to respond to such claims.
7\. **E-Discovery Volume.** E-discovery costs assume a document universe of approximately 2.5 million documents for processing and review. Significant increases in document volume, including the addition of new custodians or third-party document productions, may require a budget supplement to address additional processing and review costs.
8\. **Expert Witness Costs.** Expert witness costs are estimated at \$175,000 for two experts and may vary based on the experts ultimately retained, the scope of their engagement, and the number and complexity of expert reports and depositions required.
9\. **Post-Trial/Appeal Reserve.** A reserve of 200 hours (\$92,000) for post-trial motions and potential appellate proceedings has been included as Phase L700 to ensure comprehensive budgeting. The scope and cost of any post-trial or appellate work will depend on the outcome of the trial and the positions taken by both parties following the verdict.
10\. **Billing Rates.** All billing rates reflect 2025 standard rates effective January 1, 2025, as previously communicated to the client. No mid-year rate adjustments are anticipated or included in this budget.
11\. **No Material Changes.** The budget assumes no material changes to the litigation schedule, scope, or complexity beyond what is currently known and anticipated. Developments such as the intervention of additional parties, significant amendments to the pleadings, or extraordinary discovery disputes may necessitate a budget supplement.
**Variance Notifications.** We will promptly notify the General Counsel\'s office if any phase is projected to exceed 110% of its budgeted amount, consistent with the client\'s Outside Counsel Guidelines. Such notifications will include an explanation of the circumstances giving rise to the variance and a revised estimate for the affected phase.
**UTBMS Compliance.** All time entries will be recorded using UTBMS litigation phase and task codes, and block billing will not be used. Each time entry will describe a single task performed by a single timekeeper, with sufficient detail to permit meaningful review by the General Counsel\'s office and Lexera Solutions, Inc.
**Conflicts Certification.** Whitfield Garrett LLP certifies that it has conducted a conflicts review in accordance with its internal policies and the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct and is not aware of any conflicts of interest with respect to this matter as of the date of this submission.

Mr. Croft\'s time in L300 is focused on deposition strategy, attendance at key depositions, and oversight of the discovery plan.
During Motion Practice (L400), Mr. Croft and Ms. Okeke will bear primary responsibility for the summary judgment briefing, with Mr. Yoon providing research and drafting support. During Trial (L600), the full team will be present in the courtroom, with Mr. Croft handling opening statements, closing arguments, and examinations of key witnesses, and the associate team providing real-time research, witness management, and exhibit handling. The total hours for each timekeeper in this table reconcile to the totals set forth in the staffing model in Section 3, ensuring consistency in the allocation of professional resources across all phases of the engagement.
**[Section 8: Billing and Compliance Representations]**
Whitfield Garrett LLP will comply with Colton Beverage Holdings, Inc.\'s Outside Counsel Guidelines (Version 4.2, effective January 1, 2025) in all respects in connection with this matter. The following summarizes our billing procedures and compliance commitments:
**Invoicing.** Invoices will be submitted on a monthly basis and will be payable net 45 days from the date of submission. All invoices will be submitted electronically through Lexera Solutions, Inc., the client\'s designated legal bill review and e-billing provider.
**UTBMS Coding.** All time entries will be recorded using UTBMS litigation phase codes and task codes, ensuring that the General Counsel\'s office and Lexera Solutions, Inc. can track spending against the approved budget on a phase-by-phase basis.
**No Block Billing.** Block billing will not be used. Each time entry will reflect a single task performed by a single timekeeper, described with sufficient narrative detail to permit meaningful review. Entries that aggregate multiple tasks into a single time entry will not be submitted.
**Budget Variance Notifications.** We will provide prompt notification to the General Counsel\'s office in the event that any UTBMS phase is projected to exceed 110% of its budgeted amount. Such notifications will include an explanation of the variance and a revised estimate for the affected phase, and will be submitted before the excess spending is incurred to the extent practicable.
**No Premium Billing Arrangements.** This budget does not include any success fees, contingency arrangements, premium billing, or holdback provisions. All fees are based on hourly rates multiplied by time expended.
**Rate Communications.** Rate increases for the 2025 calendar year were communicated to the General Counsel\'s office on December 15, 2024, with an effective date of January 1, 2025. The rates reflected in this budget correspond to those communicated in the rate notification letter.
**OCG Compliance Administration.** Compliance with the OCGs, including timekeeper approvals, expense pre-approvals, and billing format requirements, will be administered in coordination with Lexera Solutions, Inc. We welcome any feedback from Lexera Solutions or the General Counsel\'s office regarding our compliance with these requirements.
**[Section 9: Conclusion and Approval Request]**
Based on our assessment of the case, including the complexity of the trade secrets claims under O.C.G.A. § 10-1-761, the substantial volume of discovery involving approximately 2.5 million documents, the anticipated motion practice, and the 8-to-10-day trial, we believe the proposed budget of \$2,397,450 (professional fees of \$1,708,950 plus expenses of \$688,500) represents a comprehensive and realistic estimate for this matter through trial conclusion.
We respectfully request that General Counsel approve this budget at your earliest convenience so that we may continue to advance the matter efficiently and in accordance with the established litigation schedule. Prompt approval will enable us to finalize vendor engagements, confirm expert witness retentions, and plan deposition logistics within the timeline established by the Court.
We are available to discuss any aspect of this budget, including phase allocations, staffing, expense projections, or any other matter of concern, at your convenience. We thank you for the opportunity to continue our representation of Colton Beverage Holdings, Inc. in this important matter.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor, Inches
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document()
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(1)
sec.top_margin = sec.bottom_margin = Inches(1)
st = doc.styles["Normal"]; st.font.name = "Calibri"; st.font.size = Pt(10.5)
for h,s in (("Heading 1",14),("Heading 2",12),("Heading 3",11)):
    doc.styles[h].font.name="Calibri"; doc.styles[h].font.size=Pt(s); doc.styles[h].font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x1F,0x3A,0x5F)

def shade(cell, color):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); sh = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    sh.set(qn("w:val"),"clear"); sh.set(qn("w:color"),"auto"); sh.set(qn("w:fill"),color); tcPr.append(sh)

def p(text="", bold=False, italic=False, size=None, align=None, style=None):
    para = doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(para, text, bold, italic, size)
    if align: para.alignment = align
    para.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    return para

def add_runs(para, text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None):
    # **bold** markup support
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i,part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part: continue
        r = para.add_run(part); r.bold = bold or (i%2==1); r.italic = italic
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)

def bullet(text, level=0):
    para = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level==0 else "List Bullet 2")
    add_runs(para, text); para.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return para

def table(headers, rows, widths=None, font=9, header_fill="1F3A5F"):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""; r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF); shade(c, header_fill)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i,v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""; add_runs(cells[i].paragraphs[0], str(v), size=font)
            if str(v).startswith("High"): shade(cells[i],"F4CCCC")
            elif str(v).startswith("Medium"): shade(cells[i],"FCE5CD")
            elif str(v).startswith("Low"): shade(cells[i],"FFF2CC")
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i,w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def issue(num, title, severity, ocg, finding, impact, action):
    h = doc.add_heading(f"{num}  {title}", level=3)
    para = doc.add_paragraph(); para.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2)
    r = para.add_run("Severity: "); r.bold=True
    r = para.add_run(severity + "     "); 
    r = para.add_run("OCG provision(s): "); r.bold=True
    para.add_run(ocg)
    para = doc.add_paragraph(); para.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); r=para.add_run("Finding. "); r.bold=True; add_runs(para, finding)
    if impact:
        para = doc.add_paragraph(); para.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); r=para.add_run("Financial impact. "); r.bold=True; add_runs(para, impact)
    para = doc.add_paragraph(); para.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(8); r=para.add_run("Required action. "); r.bold=True; add_runs(para, action)

# ---------- Header ----------
p("PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL", bold=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, size=10)
p("ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT", bold=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, size=10)
p("MEMORANDUM", bold=True, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, size=16)

        ("MATERIALS:","(1) Whitfield Garrett Litigation Matter Budget Proposal dated May 12, 2025; (2) Colton Outside Counsel Guidelines v4.2 (eff. Jan. 1, 2025) (\"OCG\"); (3) 2024 Budget vs. Actuals workbook (Mar. 15 - Dec. 31, 2024; prepared Jan. 31, 2025); (4) N. Croft rate increase notice email dated Dec. 15, 2024; (5) S. Okeke timekeeper addition request email dated Apr. 25, 2025")]
for i,(a,b) in enumerate(vals):
    hdr.rows[i].cells[0].text=""; r=hdr.rows[i].cells[0].paragraphs[0].add_run(a); r.bold=True

# ---------- I. Executive summary ----------
doc.add_heading("I. Executive Summary and Bottom Line", level=1)
p("Whitfield Garrett LLP (\"WG\") requests approval of a $2,397,450 budget ($1,708,950 fees; $688,500 expenses) covering May 1, 2025 through the end of trial. We reviewed the proposal line by line against OCG v4.2, the 2024 budget-to-actuals workbook, and the two related WG emails. **Recommendation: do not approve the budget as submitted. Return it to WG for revision under OCG Sections 5.2 and 5.4.** It does not reconcile, it contains an unauthorized L700 appellate reserve, and it is built on billing rates and staffing that the OCG does not allow. More than 80% of the expense budget also depends on pre-approvals that have not been requested.")
p("Key findings:", bold=True)
for b in [
 "**The budget does not reconcile and understates the cost.** The phase table (Section 2) totals $1,708,950. The staffing table (Section 3), which is hours times rates, totals $1,825,000. The **$116,050 difference** is neither identified nor explained, as OCG 5.2 requires. Nearly all of it sits in L300 Discovery (understated by $57,000) and L400 Motion Practice (understated by $51,200). At WG's own rates, L400 would reach 119% of its budget, past the 110% overrun threshold, before any work begins. On WG's own numbers the true request is about **$2,513,500**, plus up to about $49,500 for Boyd Whitaker's 60 unbudgeted partner hours.",
 "**Rates exceed the OCG caps and the 3% increase limit.** Croft is at $850 against an $825 cap. Okeke is at $575 against a $550 cap, a 4.5% increase. Hu is at $225 against a $200 cap. Yoon's increase is 3.66% and Novak's is 4.17%, both above 3%. WG's notice of the 2025 increases was sent December 15, 2024, **45 days after the November 1 deadline**, so the GC may deny the 2025 increases entirely (OCG 3.2(b)). Over the budgeted hours, the rate overcharge is **$63,090** if 3% increases are allowed and **$79,500** if the late increases are denied.",
 "**The paralegal was added without proper notice or approval.** WG gave one business day's notice (Friday, April 25, 2025, for a Monday, April 28 start) instead of the 10 business days required, claimed no exigency, left out required information, and proposed an over-cap rate. Her time since April 28 is not payable until she is approved (OCG 4.3). The budget includes 740 hours ($166,500) for her.",
 "**The budget includes an unauthorized post-trial/appeal reserve.** The L700 reserve of 200 hours ($92,000 stated; $95,000 at WG's own rates) was never requested by the Company. The workbook confirms that no appellate planning was requested. Under OCG 5.4, a budget with this reserve must be returned for revision.",
 "**Major expenses lack required pre-approvals.** These are: e-discovery with Clearpoint at $285,000 on a sole-source basis, with no competitive bidding and about $393,500 over the life of the matter (OCG 7.2(a)); two experts at $90,000 and $85,000, each above the $75,000 per-expert threshold (OCG 7.3(a)); and a $95,000 Silvermark mock trial and jury consulting engagement (OCG 7.7). Together these total **$555,000, or 81% of the expense budget**. Two further items are not reimbursable: **$15,000 for internal copying** (OCG 7.5 and 7.8(a)), and business-class airfare for the lead partner on domestic trips (OCG 7.4(a)).",
 "**Staffing conflicts with the attendance rules.** WG plans to have the \"full trial team\" of four attorneys at trial, but only two attorneys may attend without approval (OCG 6.5). That puts $61,750 of Yoon and Novak L600 time at risk. Partner and associate co-attendance at depositions is also planned. A second partner, Boyd Whitaker, is proposed without approval (OCG 4.2 and 4.3).",

The diversity significant-role requirement is met by Ms. Okeke at 32.7% of attorney hours (OCG 4.5). The expense table foots to $688,500, and the phase and staffing hours each foot to 3,740.",

# ---------- III. Detailed analysis ----------
doc.add_heading("III. Detailed Findings by Category", level=1)

doc.add_heading("A. Billing Rates and Rate Increases", level=2)
issue("A-1","Proposed rates exceed the OCG maximum rate caps","High","3.1, 3.2(c), App. B",
 "OCG 3.1 sets absolute ceilings for 2025: Equity Partner $825, Senior Associate $550, Mid-Level $425, Junior $375 and Paralegal $200. It states that firms \"should not propose or include rates exceeding these caps in ... budget submissions.\" Three of WG's five timekeepers are above the cap. **Croft is at $850** (cap $825). The workbook already notes that his 2024 rate was at the cap and that \"[a]ny 2025 increase would exceed the cap.\" **Okeke is at $575** (cap $550). Her 2024 rate was already at the cap; OCG 3.2(c), using the Senior Associate example, says the rate is set at the cap. **Hu is at $225** (cap $200 for all paralegal levels). Yoon ($425) and Novak ($375) equal their category caps but fail the 3% test (A-2). WG's justifications (seniority, expanded role, subject-matter expertise, \"market rates,\" what other clients pay) are exactly the factors OCG 3.1 says do not permit billing above a cap. Lexera will reduce over-cap entries automatically, and the difference cannot be recovered.",
 "Over the budgeted hours: Croft 620 x $25 = $15,500; Okeke 980 x $25 = $24,500; Hu 740 x $25 = $18,500. **Subtotal $58,500.**",
 "WG must restate Croft at no more than $825, Okeke at no more than $550 and Hu at no more than $200 throughout the budget. Any request for an exception must go to the GC in writing under the \"extraordinary circumstances\" standard of OCG 3.1. We see no basis for one.")
issue("A-2","Annual increases exceed the 3% per-timekeeper limit","High","3.2(a), 3.2(c)",
 "The 3% cap applies to each timekeeper separately, not as a team average. Measured against the 2024 approved rates in the workbook: **Okeke** goes from $550 to $575, or **4.55%**; WG labels it 4.5%. **Yoon** goes from $410 to $425, or **3.66%**; the most allowed is $422.30. **Novak** goes from $360 to $375, or **4.17%**; the most allowed is $370.80. **Croft** goes from $825 to $850, or **3.03%**: WG concedes that 3% is $849.75 and \"round[ed]\" up to $850, which is above 3%, and in any event above the cap. No detailed written justification and no advance GC approval for an increase above 3% exists. Increases for Hu cannot be measured at all, because she had no approved 2024 rate on this matter (A-5).",
 "Yoon 860 x $2.70 = $2,322; Novak 540 x $4.20 = $2,268 (in addition to A-1).",
 "If increases are allowed at all (see A-3), limit them to the lesser of 3% or the cap: Croft $825, Okeke $550, Yoon $422.30, Novak $370.80.")
issue("A-3","The 2025 rate increase notice was untimely","High","3.2(b), 3.2(d), App. B",
 "Requests for increases effective January 1 must reach the GC by November 1 of the prior year. WG's notice is dated **December 15, 2024**: 45 days late and only 17 days before the effective date, which the workbook itself acknowledges (Note 4). OCG 3.2(b) says untimely requests \"may be denied in their entirety\" and \"may be rejected without further consideration.\" WG's email states that it \"considers this notification as satisfying its obligations under ... Colton Beverage's outside counsel guidelines.\" That is incorrect. The budget then repeats, in Sections 3 and 8, Assumption 10 and Appendix A, that the rates were \"communicated\" to the client, as if communication alone made them effective.",
 "If the GC exercises the right to deny, 2025 rates revert to the 2024 approved rates: Croft $825, Okeke $550, Yoon $410, Novak $360. The fee exposure then rises to **$79,500** over budget hours (staffing-derived fees of $1,745,500 instead of $1,825,000).",
 "**GC decision point:** whether to deny the 2025 increases outright as untimely, which is the recommended position for Okeke and the associates given the cumulative non-compliance, or to accept increases limited to 3% and the caps. Either way, confirm in writing (OCG 3.2(d)). No increase is approved until written GC confirmation is issued. Retroactive billing at unapproved rates since January 1, 2025 must be reduced.")
issue("A-4","No written approval of 2025 rates; rates presented as firm \"standard\" rates","Medium","3.1, 3.3, 3.2(d)",
 "The budget calls its rates \"standard rates charged by each timekeeper for all client matters\" (Appendix A) and \"current market rates\" (Section 3). Under the OCG, only GC-approved rates within the caps are billable. Approved rates must be documented in the engagement letter, a rate schedule amendment or a written GC confirmation. Nothing provided shows any GC approval of the 2025 rates, and WG's December 2024 email only asked the GC to \"confirm receipt.\" Invoices since January 2025 may already reflect unapproved rates.",
 "",
 "Require WG to (i) confirm what rates were billed on January-April 2025 invoices, (ii) credit any amounts above the approved rates, and (iii) submit a rate schedule amendment for GC signature that reflects the rates the GC approves.")
issue("A-5","2024 base rates misstated; fictitious prior-year rate for the paralegal","Medium","3.2(a), 5.2(b)",
 "Budget Appendix A shows Yoon's 2024 rate as **$415** (a 2.4% increase). WG's own December 2024 notice and the 2024 workbook show **$410** (3.7%). Appendix A and the notice both show Novak's 2024 rate as **$365** (2.7%), but the workbook shows she billed at **$360** throughout 2024 (4.17%). By overstating the base, the increases appear to fall within 3% when they do not. Appendix A also lists a **$215 \"2024 rate\"** for Margaret Hu, with a 4.7% increase. Hu did not work on the matter in 2024: the 2024 paralegal was Lisa Ferrante at $195, and Hu joined April 28, 2025. Hu therefore has no approved prior-year rate, and her rate is governed by the $200 cap and the new-timekeeper approval process (OCG 3.3 and 4.3).",
 "",
 "Require WG to correct Appendix A to the approved 2024 rates, recompute every percentage increase, and remove the fictitious Hu 2024 rate. Ask WG to explain the discrepancies, because they bear directly on rate-compliance representations made to the Company.")

doc.add_heading("B. Staffing and Timekeepers", level=2)
issue("B-1","Paralegal Margaret Hu (\"Hsu\") was added without required notice or approval","High","4.3, 3.3, 3.1, 6.4(h)",
 "OCG 4.3 requires (a) at least 10 business days' advance written notice and (b) the GC's written approval before a timekeeper is added. WG's request was emailed **Friday, April 25, 2025 at 3:47 p.m.** for a start on **Monday, April 28**, which is one business day. The budget confirms she was \"added to the matter team effective April 28, 2025\" on April 25 notice. Compressed notice is allowed only in \"genuinely exigent circumstances\" with a contemporaneous written explanation. The reason WG gave, growth in discovery volume ahead of a September 30 deadline set long ago, is foreseeable and not exigent. The paralegal departure that created the gap was also known since January 15, 2025, more than three months earlier. The notice is also incomplete under 4.3: it gives no years of experience and no qualifications or background (WG offered only to provide them on request), and the proposed rate of $225 exceeds the cap, contrary to 4.3(iv). The name is inconsistent: the subject line and the workbook say \"Hsu\"; the email body and the budget say \"Hu.\" Nothing provided shows that GC approval was granted. Her rate must also be submitted for approval at the same time (OCG 3.3).",
 "Time billed by an unapproved timekeeper \"will not be paid\" (OCG 4.3). The budget includes **740 hours / $166,500** for her (**$148,000** at the $200 cap). Any time she spent \"getting up to speed\" on the file is non-billable (6.4(h)), because the transition was not requested by the Company.",
 "Do not treat her as an approved timekeeper on the strength of the budget. If the GC wishes to approve her going forward: require a complete 4.3 notice that confirms her legal name and gives her experience and qualifications; set her rate at no more than $200; and set an approval effective date no earlier than the GC's written approval. Time from April 28 until approval should be written off. Instruct Lexera accordingly.")
issue("B-2","Boyd Whitaker: second partner proposed without approval, and his hours left out of the totals","Medium","4.2, 4.3, 5.2(b), 6.4(h)",
 "Sections 2.3 and 4.6 say partner Boyd Whitaker \"may assist\" with summary judgment briefing for about 60 hours. Assumption 5 concedes those hours are \"not ... included in the staffing totals or fee estimates.\" Because the approved staffing plan has one partner, adding a second partner requires advance written GC approval before any billable work (OCG 4.2), plus a 10-business-day notice under 4.3 with his rate and qualifications. His rate, title (equity or non-equity) and bar year are not given. Leaving foreseeable hours out of the budget understates the cost and conflicts with 5.2(b) (every expected timekeeper must appear) and the OCG's warning against \"unduly optimistic estimates.\" His time on summary judgment also risks duplicating Croft's 140 hours and Okeke's 180 hours in L400, and his ramp-up time is non-billable under 6.4(h).",
 "60 hours x $725-$825 = **about $43,500-$49,500**, outside the budget.",
 "Require WG either to remove Whitaker or to submit a 4.2/4.3 request with his rate (at or below the applicable cap), scope and justification, and to show his hours in the staffing and phase tables with corresponding reductions elsewhere to avoid duplication.")
issue("B-3","The \"full trial team\" of four attorneys exceeds the two-attorney trial attendance limit","High","6.5, 4.1",
 "Section 2.5 says \"the full trial team will be in attendance throughout the proceedings\": Croft, Okeke, Yoon and Novak, plus Hu. Section 7 says \"the full team will be present in the courtroom.\" OCG 6.5 allows no more than two attorneys at any trial session without the GC's advance written pre-approval. No pre-approval has been requested.",
 "L600 hours for Yoon (110 x $425 = $46,750) and Novak (40 x $375 = $15,000) total **$61,750** at risk to the extent they represent courtroom attendance.",
 "Require WG to restructure L600 to two attending attorneys, with any associate support done outside the courtroom and justified. Alternatively, WG may submit a specific advance request under 6.5 explaining why a third attorney is needed for particular sessions.")
issue("B-4","Multiple attorneys planned at depositions and internal meetings","Medium","6.5, 6.4(f), 4.1",
 "Section 7 describes Croft's L300 time as including \"attendance at key depositions,\" while Okeke is responsible for \"conducting depositions.\" Without prior GC approval, only one attorney's attendance at a deposition is paid; Lexera reduces to the lowest-rate attorney. The 2024 record shows the pattern: both Croft and Okeke billed for the July 2024 Ridgewater CEO deposition. The staffing plan also contemplates broad team involvement in every phase, including L700, which increases the risk of non-billable multi-attorney internal conferences (6.4(f)).",
 "Not quantifiable from the budget; part of Croft's 120 L300 hours is at risk.",
 "Require WG to identify which depositions, if any, it proposes to staff with two attorneys and to seek advance approval for each. Otherwise budget a single attending attorney per deposition.")
issue("B-5","Work assigned at the wrong level: attorney cite-checking and binder work; administrative paralegal tasks","Medium","4.1, 6.4(c), 6.4(g)",
 "Section 4.4 assigns Ms. Novak \"cite-checking, preparation of deposition exhibit binders, and assistance with trial exhibit organization and logistics.\" Cite-checking and proofreading at attorney rates are non-billable (6.4(g)). Binder assembly and logistics belong with paralegals (4.1). Ms. Hu's scope includes \"organization and maintenance of trial binders, witness files\" and \"document management\"; filing, organizing and indexing are non-billable administrative tasks (6.4(c)). In 2024 Lexera already cut **$7,100** for administrative or clerical tasks billed at attorney rates, and Novak's 2024 entries include \"cite-checking,\" \"document indexing\" and \"filing organization.\"",
 "Not quantified; part of Novak's 540 hours and Hu's 740 hours.",
 "Require WG to remove non-billable tasks from the budget assumptions, to confirm they will not be billed, and to reassign substantive tasks to the lowest-cost qualified timekeeper.")
issue("B-6","Staffing ratio and diversity are compliant, but reporting gaps exist","Low","4.4, 4.5, 9.1(d), 9.3",
 "**Staffing efficiency ratio (compliant).** In the budget, Yoon and Novak have 1,400 of 3,000 attorney hours, or 46.67%. The 2024 actuals give (242 + 168) / 943 = 43.5%. On a cumulative basis (OCG 4.4), (410 + 1,400) / (943 + 3,000) = **45.9%**, or 45.2% if Whitaker's 60 hours are added. All of these exceed 40%. However, WG computed the ratio for the budget period only, and January-April 2025 actuals are missing, so the cumulative figure cannot be fully verified. **Diversity (compliant).** Ms. Okeke has 980 of 3,000 hours (32.67%); cumulatively about 33.2%. **Reporting gap.** Lisa Ferrante's departure (January 15, 2025) was a staffing change requiring notice within 24 hours (9.3) and reporting (9.1(d)). Instead, WG's December 15, 2024 email said that \"the firm does not currently have a paralegal assigned to this matter,\" although the workbook shows Ferrante billed on the matter every month from March through December 2024.",
 "",
 "Require cumulative ratio and diversity metrics through the most recent month in each quarterly report. Ask WG to explain the inaccurate statement about paralegal staffing and the unreported departure.")

issue("C-1","Phase-based fees do not reconcile to the staffing table ($116,050 gap, not disclosed)","High","5.2(a), 5.2(b), 5.2(e)",
 "OCG 5.2 requires the phase total to reconcile to hours times rates, and any discrepancy to be \"identified and explained in the budget narrative.\" Budgets that do not reconcile \"will be returned for revision and will not be approved.\" The Section 2 phase table totals **$1,708,950**. The Section 3 staffing table totals **$1,825,000**. The Section 7 phase-by-phase allocation, priced at WG's own rates, also totals $1,825,000. The **$116,050** gap is not mentioned. Section 7 asserts that the tables \"reconcile,\" which is true only of hours. The executive summary, the grand total and the approval request all use the lower figure, so **the headline request of $2,397,450 is understated. On WG's own rates and hours it is $2,513,500** ($1,825,000 + $688,500), before Whitaker.",
 "$116,050 understatement (and up to $165,550 including Whitaker).",
 "Return the budget. Require a single, reconciled fee build: hours by timekeeper by phase, times approved rates, with the phase table derived from it.")

issue("C-2","L300 and L400 are understated by phase, building in overruns","High","5.2, 5.3",
 "The understatement is concentrated in two phases.
